content:
maya: Thanks everyone — a few follow-ups from today's runtime section. I'll drop questions here so leadership/eng can chime in.
liam: thanks Maya — fire away.
sandra: quick one first: any ETA on the kernel scheduling refactor you showed? Will it land before Q2 infra work?
maya: @sandra the slide said 'targeting next quarter' — can we get a concrete month?
carlos: short answer: aiming for late-April cut, internal canary in mid-April. Still a couple of perf regressions to iron out.
jen: are those regressions model-specific or infra-level? wondering about rollout risk for Llama variants.
carlos: mostly infra-level (batch scheduling edge cases). We saw a tail latency bump for very short sequences when continuous batching threshold was off.
ashley: can you share the quick repro logs? that would help teams trying to run local sim.
carlos: pasted small snippet below:
```
2026-04-02T12:03:45Z serve ERROR batch_scheduler.cpp:172 - batch overflow: max_batch=32 got=40
2026-04-02T12:03:45Z kv_cache INFO cache.cpp:88 - evicted 12 prefixes (seq_len=8 avg)
```
noah: thanks — is that from the optimized kernels branch or main?
carlos: optimized-kernels/mlopt-2026 branch. The kernel microcode changed how we assign micro-batches for short sequences.
liam: another roadmap question: will the batching/caching tuning be managed by Redwood Optimize autopilot or will teams need to opt in manually?
jen: +1 — ops teams want to know if we force policy changes during canaries.
maya: leadership note: we will not auto-flip customer configs. Optimize will suggest and we provide a one-click apply in Console, but not forced.
sandra: good. can we expose a simulated cost/latency delta before applying?
ashley: that's in the plan. Console mock will show projected p95 and token-cost delta from historical traces.
carlos: operational note: when we flip the scheduling refactor, we will enable a compatibility mode so dedicated clusters can opt into the new scheduler per pool.
noah: what about KV cache invalidation semantics? will model-serving keep the same per-request semantics or change to time-based eviction?
enc-large: (system mis-typed name)
jen: lol small typo.
noah: re-asking: will cache eviction be time-based?
carlos: plan is to keep exact semantics but add a pluggable TTL. Default stays as-is (LRU by capacity).
liam: rollout plan question for leadership: if the kernel change causes a 5% regression for some customers, do we have an automated rollback trigger?
maya: yes — Console will watch p99/p95 and we have automatic fallback to previous kernel for any pool exceeding configured SLO thresholds (opt-in per customer for Dedicated/Private). Hosted has default thresholds.
sandra: helpful. small ask: can we get a short doc with recommended SLO thresholds for common workloads (chat vs embeddings) so teams can set sane alerts?
maya: noted — I'll ask Product to publish a short checklist.
carlos: last technical note: devs, please run the new micro-benchmark harness (tools/perf/harness) against your models. It catches most scheduling regressions.
ashley: link?
carlos: https://internal.redwood/tools/perf/harness — README has commands. Example: `./harness --model llama-13b --seq-distribution short`
noah: could we add a Canary tag to the harness output so CI can detect regressions?
carlos: yes will add `--canary` flag.
jen: one more product question from the thread: do kernel improvements require model graph changes (e.g., attention kernels needing graph ops) or are they runtime-only?
carlos: runtime-only for our current plan. If we need graph-level hooks we'll call it out and schedule with model owners.
liam: thanks all. If leadership or infra wants a follow-up sync with eng-runtime, we can carve 20m next week.
maya: let's do Tue 10am PT. I'll drop a calendar invite. :calendar: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Rollout scheduled: kernel-scheduler-v2 -> canary pool (mid-Apr) by carlos. See /deploys/182 for details.
jen: thanks deploy-bot.
liam: tagging this resolved for now — will reopen if new questions. :white_check_mark:
